text.p: Defending champions Warwickshire ended Derbyshire's dream of a first county championship in 60 years on Saturday with an unexpected four wicket victory at Derby.
Derbyshire are now 25 points behind the leaders Leicestershire and can not overtake their Midlands' rivals in the final game of the season.
Warwickshire, chasing 267 to win on the third day of their four-day match, slipped to 84 for five before Derbyshire's front line bowlers, minus the injured Dominic Cork, began to tire.
Trevor Penny, who finished unbeaten on 83, marshalled the lower order superbly and he was ably assisted by Ashley Giles (67 not out) who scored his fourth championship century of the season.
Derbyshire's Australian captain Dean Jones paid tribute to his players afterwards.
"I was so proud of the boys at the end," he said. "They walked off the pitch with their heads held high.
"There has been a lot of improvement and the team spirit has been brilliant."
Surrey's chances of a first championship since 1971 were hampered by the smallest man in county cricket.
Tony Cottey, 1.6 metres high, struck 64 not out as Glamorgan took their second innings to 218 for three, 111 runs in front and in a position to set Surrey a stiff victory target.
